Authorities and political actors run a smart selfish maneuver, leveraging security incidents as a pretext to restrict independent reporting and project institutional control.

The Unavoidable Lie: Sweeping media bans are neutral administrative updates rather than retaliatory censorship.

It is deeply unsettling to watch public safety incidents get entangled with political retaliation. When trust breaks down, fear takes the place of open dialogue, leaving everyone feeling vulnerable.

There was a dramatic security scare outside the White House on Saturday afternoon after a man drove onto a sidewalk and demanded to speak to President Donald Trump, triggering a rapid response from the Secret Service.

Law enforcement and military personnel descended on the area near Lafayette Square after the vehicle mounted the sidewalk at 16th and H streets Northwest shortly after 12:15pm.

The unidentified driver was detained and photographed in handcuffs as officers surrounded and searched his vehicle.

The man had been demanding to speak directly to Trump, but the president was not even at the White House at the time.

Trump was spending Saturday at Camp David in Maryland, according to his public schedule.

Politico, CNN and MS NOW journalists have been denied access to the White House after US President Donald Trump announced he was banning the outlets.

An MS NOW reporter and a photographer tried entering the White House grounds on Saturday morning, but their badges would not scan and an officer confiscated them, the outlet reported.

Both CNN and Politico also said Saturday morning that their reporters were denied access and had their badges seized.

Trump said on Friday he was barring all three major US media outlets from the White House, accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
